title: Dimension drop for a principal Cartier subscheme of an affine variety
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $A$ be a nonzero finitely generated $k$-algebra such that $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-integral-scheme] is integral and of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. If $f\in A$ is nonzero and not a unit, then the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}(A/(f))$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-scheme] has Krull dimension $\dim(\operatorname{Spec}(A))-1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

source.place: Tags 00KV and 00KW (Krull principal ideal and height theorems), together with the finite-type dimension formula Tag 02FX

proof.text: Since Spec(A) is integral, A is a domain, so the nonzero element f is a nonzerodivisor. Since f is not a unit, (f) is a proper ideal, A/(f) is nonzero and there is a maximal ideal of A containing f. Since Spec(k) is locally Noetherian and Spec(A) is of finite type over k, Spec(A) is locally Noetherian [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], so the ring A is Noetherian and all localizations A_m at maximal ideals are Noetherian local rings.

source.place: Tags 00KV and 00KW, hypotheses for the principal ideal theorem

proof.text: For every maximal ideal m of A containing f, localize at m. The image of f lies in the maximal ideal of A_m and remains a nonzerodivisor (A_m is a domain). Applying the local principal-ideal dimension theorem [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] gives dim(A_m/fA_m) + 1 = dim(A_m). Since A is a finite-type k-domain, dim(A_m) = dim(A), a non-negative integer, for every maximal ideal m [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring]. Under the canonical identification A_m/fA_m = (A/(f))_{m/(f)}, every maximal ideal n = m/(f) of A/(f) therefore has dim((A/(f))_n) = dim(A) - 1.

source.place: Tag 00KW after localization, with the finite-type domain equality dim A_m = dim A (Tags 00OS, 00P0)

proof.text: For any scheme the Krull dimension of its underlying space is the supremum of the dimensions of its local rings [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings]. Apply this to X = Spec(A) and Y = Spec(A/(f)), both nonempty. Every prime p of a ring lies in a maximal ideal m, and the local ring at p is a localization of the local ring at m, so dim of the local ring at p is at most dim of the local ring at m (prime correspondence for localization); hence each supremum is attained over maximal ideals. By step 2 and lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring, all local rings of X at maximal ideals have dimension dim(A) and all local rings of Y at maximal ideals have dimension dim(A) - 1 (and Y has at least one maximal ideal by step 1). Hence dim(Spec(A)) = dim(A) and dim(Spec(A/(f))) = dim(A) - 1 = dim(Spec(A)) - 1.
